label: EU(7)-PIM: oral terbutaline
title: Oral terbutaline in an older person
statement: Oral terbutaline (tablets or liquid by mouth) is on the EU(7)-PIM list of medicines to avoid in older people, because it carries a higher risk of side effects than the inhaled form. The inhaled form is the suggested alternative. The list also advises a smaller dose when kidney function is moderately reduced and advises avoiding the medicine when kidney function is severely reduced.

plain_summary: Terbutaline taken by mouth has more side effects than terbutaline breathed in, so a review is worth asking for in an older person.

medicine_groups.name: Oral terbutaline
medicine_groups.note: Tablets and liquids taken by mouth count. Inhalers do not count, for example Bricanyl Turbuhaler, and neither do nebuliser solutions or injections. No Australian brand of oral terbutaline is listed here because none is known with confidence, so histories may show the ingredient name only.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a person aged 65 or over is supplied terbutaline to take by mouth as a tablet or liquid. If age is missing and the supply otherwise qualifies, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is 65 or older. A recorded age below 65 gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Kidney disease is unknown if there is no relevant diagnosis in the record. Kidney function is unknown if there is no relevant dated result. The reason for choosing oral terbutaline, actual use and supplies from other pharmacies may also be unknown.
ask_the_gp: Whether the oral terbutaline is still needed or an inhaled form could be used instead, and whether the dose suits the patient's kidney function.
